messages:
anna_support: Hey team — customer on Dedicated (VPC) reporting intermittent 403s when calls are proxied via their edge LB -> internal F5 -> our dedicated gateway. Only happens for requests originating from their SSO flow (Azure AD opaque token handed off from their IdP). Works sometimes, then 403s for a minute.
raj_engineer: Can you paste a minimal repro and any gateway logs? Which header are they forwarding? Authorization: Bearer or a cookie?
anna_support: They're forwarding a POST with a cookie: SSO_SESSION=opaque_blob (long base64-ish string ~6-8KB). Their edge does cookie->Authorization rewrite (cookie value -> Authorization: Bearer <token>) before hitting our gateway. Attached the gateway error logs (snippet below).
anna_support: ```
[2024-11-05T12:02:13Z] req_id=abcd1234 status=403 path=/v1/generate reason="auth failed: missing token" peer_addr=10.0.5.12
[2024-11-05T12:02:14Z] req_id=abcd1235 status=200 path=/v1/health
[2024-11-05T12:03:01Z] req_id=abcd1260 status=403 path=/v1/generate reason="auth failed: token truncated"
```
mike_infra: "token truncated" is interesting. Do we have Envoy/Ingress logs showing header sizes or any header validation errors? Could be header size/fragmentation across proxies. Which LB type at the edge? NLB or ALB?
anna_support: Customer uses AWS NLB (proxy protocol enabled) -> F5 LTM -> internal reverse proxy -> our dedicated gateway (Envoy). We suspect the rewrite happens on the F5.
raj_engineer: Two hypotheses: 1) The F5 or NLB does chunking/fragmentation and we hit Envoy's max header size; truncated header becomes invalid and we return 403. 2) Some proxy replaces Authorization with an empty header when cookie is enormous, and our auth filter returns 403 specifically for truncated/invalid tokens.
jenna_security: Also worth checking token format: Azure AD opaque tokens can be long (SAML/Assertion wrapped). If the rewrite creates an oversized single header > 8KB, Envoy may drop or truncate it depending on buffer settings.
anna_support: Customer ran a curl reproducer for us:
anna_support: ```
curl -v -X POST https://dedicated.example.customer/v1/generate \
  -H "Host: dedicated.example.customer" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(printf '%s' \"$SSO_COOKIE\")" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
``` 
anna_support: With the full cookie -> header it failed 100% of attempts. If they base64-trimmed the token to ~2KB it started succeeding.
mike_infra: That strongly points to header-size / buffer limits. We should check Envoy: 'max_request_headers_kb' and the listener buffer. Also check if upstream (our runtime) has a token size cap when parsing credentials.
raj_engineer: Can you collect raw tcpdump between F5 and gateway for one failed and one successful attempt? Also enable debug logging for the auth filter: set REDWOOD_AUTH_LOG_LEVEL=debug for the dedicated gateway node.
anna_support: I asked the customer to capture tcpdump and to temporarily bypass the F5 rewrite (send token directly as header). They confirmed: direct header from client -> success. Rewrite -> sometimes truncated.
jenna_security: If this is reproducible with rewrite, short term mitigation: recommend the customer switch to sending a short-lived opaque reference token (ID -> look up session server) or use a signed JWT with smaller footprint. Also they can increase Envoy header buffer on their dedicated gateway config: listener.http_connection_manager.max_request_headers_kb (default 64KB? double-check).
raj_engineer: I don't love recommending config changes in production without eng-infra review. I'll reproduce locally with an F5 mock: run an NLB -> HAProxy that does cookie-to-header rewrite with a ~6KB value and hit a dedicated gateway dev replica with current envoy settings.
ci-bot: New support ticket created: SUP-2024-1872. Escalation set to P2. Assigned: raj_engineer, mike_infra.
mike_infra: Reproducer notes: Envoy 1.23 defaults to 60KB for headers? If their cookie encodes SAML assertion with lots of whitespace/base64, actual effective header bytes might be > 8KB for single header chunking at some proxies. F5 may be doing chunk boundary cutting.
raj_engineer: Found something local: HAProxy with http-use-proxy-header and default buffers will break up very long headers and some downstream servers treat continuation as separate header fragments leading to parsing as different header lines (Envoy then treats as invalid Authorization). I'll open a PR to add more robust header reassembly logging in our auth filter.
anna_support: Customer asks for workarounds they can apply now. Suggested list:
- Move to smaller token (reference token) or short-lived JWT
- Disable cookie->header rewrite and send a short Authorization header from client
- Ask F5 admin to increase max header size / preserve header integrity
- As temporary provider-side change: increase max_request_headers_kb for their dedicated gateway (requires Dedicated config change and approval)
raj_engineer: I'll create an internal ticket for eng-infra to evaluate adding defensive handling for oversized Authorization headers (reject with clearer log + 4xx vs 403, and better metric). Tagging @mike_infra for infra follow-up.
mike_infra: For the time being, I recommended customer to force gzip of the cookie payload (if they can) which reduced size and avoided truncation in their tests.
jenna_security: Also confirm that accepting larger headers doesn't open DoS vector. We'll need rate/size limits and monitoring.
anna_support: Customer will try smaller token and report back. Marking this thread as escalated. I'll attach tcpdumps to SUP-2024-1872 once they send them.
raj_engineer: Thanks — I'll keep this thread updated after local repro. If we confirm Envoy buffer issue we'll coordinate a Dedicated config rollout change path.
anna_support: cc @mike_infra @jenna_security — closing for now until customer attachments are in the ticket. :thumbsup:
